I'll calculate the sum of the decimal digits of 64! independently.
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Calculate 64!
factorial_64 = math.factorial(64)

# Convert to string to get the digits
factorial_str = str(factorial_64)

# Print the factorial value
print(f"64! = {factorial_str}")
print(f"Number of digits: {len(factorial_str)}")

# Sum the digits
digit_sum = sum(int(digit) for digit in factorial_str)

print(f"Sum of digits: {digit_sum}")

# Let's also verify by showing the digits
print(f"\nDigits: {', '.join(factorial_str)}")
EOF
</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Let me verify this calculation once more to be absolutely certain:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Calculate 64!
factorial_64 = math.factorial(64)

# Method 1: Direct sum
digits = [int(d) for d in str(factorial_64)]
sum_of_digits = sum(digits)

print(f"64! = {factorial_64}")
print(f"Digits list: {digits}")
print(f"Sum of digits (Method 1): {sum_of_digits}")

# Method 2: Verification using modulo arithmetic to double-check
verification_sum = 0
temp = factorial_64
while temp > 0:
    verification_sum += temp % 10
    temp //= 10

print(f"Sum of digits (Method 2 - verification): {verification_sum}")
EOF
</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
